INPUT DATA: {"lessonId":"carbonyl-redox","title":"Aldehyde oxidation and hydride reduction","fullNote":"

Aldehydes can be oxidized to carboxylic acids; ordinary ketones resist analogous oxidation without C–C cleavage. NaBH4 and LiAlH4 reduce aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols. Hydride adds first, then oxygen is protonated in workup or by the medium. Suitable aqueous KMnO4 or Cr(VI) reagents (CrO3/acid or dichromate/acid) oxidize aldehydes.
